AR-04.note: search field filters on each keystroke (title and URL, case-insensitive, partial words, every word) using the Archive store's keys (history queryTerms/urlKeyOf); typing on narrows the last answer; Enter restores and shows the top or highlighted match; ⌘F focuses it. The command bar's Archived results search the whole Archive store of the profile, not only the recent entries kept in state

AR-05.note: Restore (hover button, Enter, row menu, several selected) puts tabs at the top of their Space's Today in order, with their tab id and back/forward history when the profile matches (never across profiles); routing rule > origin Space > current Space; toast with Go to Space when it lands elsewhere; command bar restores without a jump. A row click previews (AR-06) instead of restoring. Undoing Delete Folder after the Space changed profile also follows the new profile (W3)

AR-06.note: a row click opens its page in a Peek over the Library (the Peek component, its open and close motion); the entry stays archived. ⌘W and Esc close only the Peek and the Library takes the keys back (Enter then restores that row); Open as Tab (⌘O) opens it as a tab and keeps the entry; closing a preview, or a reopen of it, archives no second entry. Missing: a Restore button in the Peek card (peek lane). The Peek carries overlay.archiveEntry and archive.restorePreview restores and closes it. With no tab to preview over (an empty Space), a click opens the page in a new tab

AR-07.note: Clear Archive… from the Archive entry’s right-click menu in the Library, Archive → Clear Archive… (macOS app menu) and the command bar; always asks in the Library first (Cancel has the focus, Esc cancels), says it can’t be undone and that browsing history is kept; clears the profile shown, and the cleared pages leave the disk at once (the log is rewritten). Delete (a row’s menu, or Delete for the selected rows) shows a toast whose Undo puts the entries back with their history for a minute

AR-08.note: settings.archiveKeepDays, default 30; 30 Days / 90 Days / 1 Year / Forever from the Archive entry’s menu in the Library and Archive → Keep Archived Tabs For (macOS) until Settings exist. A shorter time that would delete entries asks first, in the Library, saying how many (Cancel keeps them all and the time as it was). Purged once the Archive is read at launch, hourly, and at once when a shorter time is confirmed; browsing history is not touched

AR-09.note: ⌘⇧T and ⌘Z walk back through closes with full history (TB-07, TB-18); ⌘Z also shows the tab again when it was the one shown; a closed Peek comes back through the same key (PK-10, peek lane). A page closed in the last 10 minutes keeps its history rank in the command bar (as the archived row). macOS File menu: Reopen Closed Tab and a Recently Closed submenu of the last 10; on every platform the Archive toolbar has a Recently Closed menu. Neither list shows a tab of a private or deleted profile

AR-10.note: History stays a Library section until Orbit has internal pages (D39), not a page in a tab. ⌘Y (Ctrl+H), Archive → View History (macOS) and the command bar open it next to the Archive: every visit of the current profile from the history store, newest first by day, virtualised and paged, with search (all words, title or address). A row opens its page in a new tab (⌘-click or middle-click: behind the Library); its × or its menu (Open in New Tab, Open in Background, Copy Link, Remove from History) removes every visit to the page. Clearing the Archive leaves it alone

AR-11.note: Backups of the whole sidebar (Spaces, each profile’s Favorites, pinned and Today tabs, folders, split views; no private profiles) in userData/backups, one JSON file each: taken within 5 minutes of a sidebar change (only when it differs from the newest; browsing alone never makes one), once 30 s after launch, before every restore, and with Back Up Now. Kept: the newest 10 of today, then the newest of each of the 10 days before, of each week of the month before that and of each 30 days of the year before that; a deleted profile’s Favorites, Spaces and tabs are taken out of every backup. Help → Restore Data… (macOS) and the command bar open the Backups section of the Library: a dated list (day headings, time, Spaces and tabs; a file that can’t be read is listed as such, without Restore); Restore… asks first, then puts the sidebar back: tabs in both keep their page, tabs only in the backup come back asleep (with the page and history the Archive kept for them, leaving the Archive), tabs opened since go to the Archive, Spaces added since go; private windows and their tabs are left alone; Favorites over 12 go to Today (D33). When the sidebar can’t be backed up first, nothing changes. Each restore is one step on the sidebar’s undo stack (TB-18): the toast’s Undo or ⌘Z, also in the Library, puts back the sidebar it replaced, a second ⌘Z goes further back and ⌘⇧Z restores again; earlier steps stay. After an undo, a window moved off a removed Space stays where it went, and the pages come back asleep
